Subject: Billing unit alignment for HelixHealth pilot

Hi Sara / David,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the product fit looks great. I attached a first-pass SOW and a short "context-metering" cheat sheet that shows how we count units for different call patterns. Before we send a formal commercial, can we align on two points that will materially affect pricing and the pilot discount:

1) What you expect to be the dominant call pattern for the pilot: short intent-classification calls (<= 128 tokens), multi-turn chat with history (1–10k tokens of context), or long-batch inference for document parsing (10–50k)?
2) Whether you need per-conversation KV-cache affinity (we can credit reused cache hits) versus per-request atomic token counts. Cache affinity reduces billed tokens substantially for chat-heavy usage but requires a pinned routing policy.

High level suggestion: for a 3-month pilot we typically propose a blended unit with a 10% pilot discount and a minimum monthly commitment set to the first-month forecast. But if HelixHealth expects high reuse (chat sessions with repeated prefixes), we can structure a prefix-reuse credit and deeper pilot discount in exchange for a 6-week usage checkpoint and commit.

Please review the attached SOW (HLX-Harvest_SOW_v1.pdf) — it includes two pricing options and an example invoice for mixed call patterns. If you prefer, I can walk through the invoice examples on a short call.

Next steps: confirm call pattern above and whether your security/procurement team requires any special billing language for amortization of credits.

Vanessa —

Thanks for this and for the SOW. Quick answers up front: our pilot will be two-sided: (A) clinician chat assistant — multi-turn with history reused heavily (typical active context 2–4k, sometimes 8–10k for complex cases), and (B) nightly batch document extraction (20–40k) used for indexing. On (B) we expect fewer repeats so caching is less valuable.

A couple of specific questions:
- How do you apply rounding/minimums on short bursts (e.g., the clinician assistant may generate many 40–200 token replies during a shift)? Do you round up to a per-call quantum or prorate across the session?
- If we opt for prefix-reuse credits, how are credits reconciled when a session moves between pinned and non-pinned routing (e.g., clinician moves region or uses mobile)?
- Can we get an example invoice that mixes streaming (per-call) billing and batch (per-1000-token) billing? The SOW has a sample but some line items were unclear.

Also cc'd our procurement contact David who will handle contract redlines.

Sara — thanks, this is really helpful context. Short answers here and Karthik included a technical note below.

- Rounding/minimums for short bursts: our default is per-call quantum of 16 tokens for streaming replies, with per-session aggregation for long-lived chat windows. In practice that means short replies are rounded up to the nearest 16-token quantum, but if the same session generates many small replies within a rolling 30-minute window we amortize and invoice against the session aggregate (reduces overbilling for high-turn interactions). We call this the "session rollup" policy and it is reflected in SOW option B (see invoice example).

- Prefix-reuse credits across routing: credits are issued only when the request is routed to the same KV affinity slot for the session id. If a session moves regions we have two fallback options: 1) replicate KV warm state (adds operational cost), or 2) forgo prefix credits and fall back to atomic billing for that request. For pilots we can accept a small reconciliation tolerance (we net credits monthly and allow a 3% tolerance band for lost affinity).

- Mixed invoice example: option A in the SOW is per-1000-token batch pricing for pipeline jobs and per-call quantum for streaming. Option B is a blended monthly minimum with separate invoice lines for batch tokens, streaming quanta, and prefix-credit adjustments. I've attached the cheat sheet as a quick reference.

Proposed concession for pilot: 12% pilot discount on blended unit pricing + one-time credit equal to unused minimums at the end of month two (to make your team comfortable with initial forecasting). We would include an "usage checkpoint" at week 6 to optionally adjust commitment with a pro-rata true-up.

David — happy to take any procurement questions; Marissa is on this thread to align on invoicing wording and the minimum/true-up clause.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jun 28, 2027 at 07:43 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Vanessa / Sara — short technical note to clarify how credits are computed and delivered:
>
> - Token accounting: we meter raw input+output tokens before compression. For batched jobs we apply a per-batch compression factor (customer-visible) that reduces billed tokens; streaming calls are metered at the frame level then rounded to the nearest quantum.
> - KV/prefix credits: we record a prefix hash per session and attribute cache hits to the session id. Credits are computed as: billed_tokens_without_cache - billed_tokens_with_cache. Credits are applied as a separate negative invoice line at month end to avoid per-request complexity.
> - Rounding edgecases: for multi-model fallbacks (primary quantized model -> fallback full model) we bill the primary until fallback is triggered and then bill an incremental delta for fallback compute; token rounding applies independently on each model path.
>
> If Helix wants, we can add telemetry to the pilot dashboard showing billed_tokens vs raw_tokens so you can reconcile expectations in near real time.
>
> -Karthik

Sara / David — two operational fixes we recommend adding to the SOW to avoid surprises:

1) Telemetry & checkpointing: add a week-6 usage checkpoint with exported sample invoices (automated) and a dashboard showing raw vs billed tokens by call type. This is where we reconcile prefix credits and give you a proposed adjustment to the minimum.

2) Affinity fallback language: include an exception path that allows for mobile/regional fallback without immediate loss of service — the fallback will forfeit prefix credits for affected requests but continue to serve. We recommend a monthly reconciliation tolerance (3%) and an escalation path if the tolerance is exceeded.

If you're comfortable with these two additions we'll update the SOW and DocuSign link and greenlight the pilot.
